clue.text: Preferable and fair, too

parts.note: fair means just, as in a just decision
too means as well, in addition

explanation.surface: Someone weighs an option that is both better and fair into the bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it is better to do something is saying it would be no bad idea, so preferable fits.

clue.text: Where old lag going astray is given another spell?

definitions.text: Where old lag going astray is given another spell?

parts.words: Where old lag going astray is given another spell?
parts.note: an old lag is a habitual convict who goes astray again and gets another term inside; also the old spelling of the prison word is given a different spelling

explanation.surface: A hardened criminal reoffends and is sentenced again.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell means a prison term but also points to spelling: the British form GAOL is spelt differently in the version entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Prison is where a reoffending convict serves a further term.

clue.text: Egyptian attendant turning up in Eastern garb

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Iras is one of Cleopatra's attendants in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra

explanation.surface: A servant from Egypt arrives in oriental dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The sari is the draped garment worn by women in South Asia.

clue.text: When to remember the calendar — start of November

definitions.text: When to remember the calendar — start of November

parts.words: When to remember the calendar — start of November
parts.note: the calendar here is the church's roll of saints, all commemorated together on the first of November

explanation.surface: A reminder to check your diary at the start of November.
explanation.definitionFit: This feast on the first of November honours every saint in the church calendar.

clue.text: Like some fabrics in women's cooking compartment

parts.note: W is an abbreviation for women, as on clothing labels
an oven is the enclosed compartment of a cooker

explanation.surface: Cloth is put in the oven for women.
explanation.definitionFit: Many textiles are made by interlacing threads on a loom.

clue.text: Famous aviator takes singer over mountain, gaining height

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written over another comes before it

parts.note: Jenny Lind was the famous nineteenth-century Swedish soprano
berg is Germanic for mountain, as in iceberg

explanation.surface: A celebrated pilot flies a singer over a mountain, climbing as he goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lindbergh made the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight in 1927.

clue.text: Agreed to dispatch engineers over the hill

indicators.note: to dispatch something is to send it away, so these letters are removed from the word before

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps

explanation.surface: A group consents to send its engineers off over a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove RE from AGREED and AGED is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the hill is an idiom for old, past one's best years.

clue.text: Occupation of gentlemen-at-arms, historically?

parts.note: gentlemen was the old euphemism for smugglers, and these gentlemen dealt in arms, smuggling weapons

explanation.surface: The traditional duty of the royal bodyguard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gentlemen-at-Arms are the sovereign's ceremonial bodyguard, but smugglers were also called gentlemen, so these are smugglers of weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Smuggling weapons illegally across borders is the trade meant.

clue.text: Place associated with Hardy, Arnold, or Chesterton, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A town linked with literary figures such as Hardy, Arnold or Chesterton.
explanation.walkthrough: The list of writers suggests all three are linked to the place, but only Hardy is the definition; Arnold and Chesterton supply the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy lived near the Dorset county town, which he fictionalised as Casterbridge.

clue.text: One runs about to get bolt of material? Not at all!

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
re is Latin for about, concerning
to levant is an old word meaning to bolt or abscond, especially leaving debts unpaid

explanation.surface: Someone dashes off for a bolt of cloth, then shouts that it is no such thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt of material' looks like a roll of cloth; it splits, with 'bolt' giving LEVANT and 'of material? Not at all!' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not material to a matter is beside the point, without bearing on it.

clue.text: Pound's writing for schoolchildren, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a one-pound coin or note is slang a single unit of sterling
writing is one of the three Rs taught at school: reading, writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: Ezra Pound's books written for children, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound's' looks like the poet Ezra Pound; it is the money, with 's as a link meaning is. Writing is a single one of the three Rs, so it is 'one R'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound note or coin is slang for a single unit of money; writing is a single member of the three Rs of schooling.

clue.text: Deplorably dealt with drug for young thief

indicators.note: deplorably means badly, so the letters that follow are mangled

explanation.surface: A dealer handled drugs disgracefully for a young criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two fodder runs; 'for', which looks like a link, is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's young pickpocket in Oliver Twist has become a byword for a juvenile thief.

clue.text: Artist wins Parliamentary seat, perhaps, once

parts.note: to win something is to gain it
a borough was formerly a town sending its own member to Parliament, as in rotten boroughs

explanation.surface: A painter is elected to Parliament in the old days.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gainsborough was the eighteenth-century English portrait and landscape painter.

clue.text: One goes on board, often, before fare's been laid down

definitions.text: One goes on board, often, before fare's been laid down

parts.words: One goes on board, often, before fare's been laid down
parts.note: board is a table and fare is food: a cover spread over the table before the meal is served

explanation.surface: A passenger boards before paying the fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' and 'fare' suggest travel; board means a dining table and fare the food on it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the linen cover laid on a dining table before the meal.

clue.text: Cobbled together? One's better without it

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for better surrounds the other piece

parts.note: improved means made better
one's is read as one is, giving I and S

explanation.surface: Something is knocked together hastily, and you would be better off without it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to 'One's': better (IMPROVED) placed outside it, IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cobbled together is made up on the spot from whatever is to hand.

clue.text: One crossing the floor? After a vote, one's dismissed by head of department

indicators.note: after says the next piece comes behind the first two pieces

parts.note: a cross, X, is the mark made on a ballot paper when voting

indicators.note: one is dismissed, that is taken out, from the word for head of department

parts.note: a minister is the head of a government department
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An MP crosses the floor of the House, then after a vote is sacked from a ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing the floor' suggests an MP changing party; it is a carpet lying across a floor. MINISTER without I gives MINSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An Axminster is a type of woven carpet, which stretches across a floor.

clue.text: Gipsy who's presumably broad-minded

definitions.meaning: a gipsy is one of a people who move from place to place
travel is said to broaden the mind, so one who journeys should be open-minded

explanation.surface: A gipsy is supposed to be tolerant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romany or other itinerant is called this; travel is proverbially said to broaden the mind.

clue.text: Endlessly polish book-end

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to polish is to give something a finish

explanation.surface: Someone buffs a bookend over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: Finis is Latin for end, often printed at the close of a book.

clue.text: House found among grounds

definitions.meaning: the House of ... is the upper chamber of Parliament
... is a London cricket ground, home of the MCC

explanation.surface: A house discovered in a park.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lords is shorthand for the upper chamber of Parliament; Lord's is London's famous cricket ground.

clue.text: Terribly bald? No, she has a fair amount of hair

definitions.text: Terribly bald? No, she has a fair amount of hair

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are mangled and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A woman is far from bald, having a fine head of light hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with very pale, greyish fair hair is described this way.

clue.text: Principle involved in pact over meat?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rule governs an agreement about buying meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits: buyer beware applies to any purchase, meat included.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin legal maxim, let the buyer beware, is a principle of trade.

clue.text: Penny isn't enough for the coloured stuff?

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A penny will not buy enough dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint is the coloured liquid brushed onto surfaces.

clue.text: Female judge in islands, a Pacific group

indicators.note: in says the judge piece goes inside the islands piece

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island, so two I's for islands

explanation.surface: A woman judge is posted to a group of Pacific islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiji is a nation made up of over three hundred islands in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Reason to include English milk product

indicators.note: to include means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: why means the reason, as in the whys and wherefores

explanation.surface: An argument for adding English dairy produce.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the watery liquid left after milk curdles in cheesemaking.

clue.text: Forcefully remove leader from tournament

indicators.note: the leader, the first letter, is taken from the word for tournament

parts.note: a joust was a medieval tournament of knights on horseback

explanation.surface: The front-runner is ejected from a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: JOUST minus its first letter J leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject someone by force from a position is to expel them.

clue.text: Swimmers with water wings?

parts.note: not children with inflatable arm bands but sea creatures whose fins work like wings over the water

explanation.surface: Learners paddling with inflatable armbands.
explanation.definitionFit: These ocean fish glide above the waves on large wing-like fins.

clue.text: Place of concealment he and I had entered

indicators.note: one piece entered another means it goes inside it

parts.note: taken as written
I had is contracted to I'd

explanation.surface: Two people came into a hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is a screened shelter for watching birds or game unseen.

clue.text: Ratify rent changes for a group of American students

indicators.note: changes means the letters of the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Students approve a change to their rent.
explanation.definitionFit: In American colleges a fraternity is a male students' society, often with a shared house.
